theme: plate identity TEE OWNEDBY SAMEINODE EQFILE dual probe

tests.name: tee
tests.cmd: TEE body keep LAST; file matches VAL

tests.name: chain
tests.cmd: TEE+HAS needle same process; miss REQUIRE

weaknesses.title: SAMEINODE vs EQFILE dual — agents conflate hardlink with content twin
weaknesses.detail: COPY makes EQFILE=1 SAMEINODE=0. After WRITEATOMIC on shared plate, EQFILE may fail while agents still think links share. No combined SAME_OR_EQ helper.

weaknesses.title: TEE vs WRITE LAST semantics undocumented for chains
weaknesses.detail: WRITE often leaves path-ish LAST; TEE keeps body. Agents mixing WRITE then HAS on LAST fail silently.
weaknesses.repro: WRITE then HAS LAST vs TEE then HAS LAST

weaknesses.title: OWNEDBY is euid-only — no ACL/group-write nuance
weaknesses.detail: Shared plates writable by group still OWNEDBY=0 for non-owner euid. Agents over-deny.

weaknesses.title: FILEUID/GID numeric only — no username resolve
weaknesses.detail: Agents cannot stamp owner=alice without shell getent.

weaknesses.title: HAS substring false friends in TEE chain
weaknesses.detail: HAS ready matches status=ready and not_ready. No word-boundary.

weaknesses.title: SAMEINODE path-miss vs not-same both need care
weaknesses.detail: OK=0 miss; OK=1 LAST_N=0 different inodes. Easy to require same and get probe fail.

workarounds: Always dual-probe SAMEINODE and EQFILE for share health
Prefer TEE when chaining HAS/GREP on body
OWNEDBY for strict private plates only

TEE as default WRITE mode option
